$\xi \preceq_{\text{st}} \eta$ if and only if $q_\xi(u) \leq q_\eta(u)$ for all $u \in (0, 1)$,

A trivial H-Galois extension over $k$ means that the H-Galois extension $A$ is isomorphic to $H$ itself as an H-comodule algebra. According to Proposition A.1 in the document, when $k$ is an algebraically closed field, any H-Galois extension over $k$ is necessarily trivial. 

An H-Galois extension is defined as a non-zero H-comodule algebra $A = (A,\rho_A)$ such that the map $A \otimes A \to A \otimes H$, $a \otimes b \mapsto a\rho_A(b)$ is an isomorphism. In the trivial case, this extension $A$ doesn't just become isomorphic to $H$ after some base field extension (as would be the case for a general H-Galois extension, which is a "twisted form" of $H$), but is already isomorphic to $H$ over the base field $k$ itself.
